extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (registered agents/attorneys), respondents and their counsel, and USPTO OED staff handling disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order approving a settlement that resolves disciplinary charges against a registered patent practitioner, setting forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, sanctions (suspension stayed and probation), procedures for lifting the stay, publication and notice obligations, and ancillary consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and authority to approve settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over the matter and authority to approve the proposed settlement agreement pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement approval must be made by the Under Secretary/Director under the cited statutory and regulatory provisions; the Final Order implements the approved settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Disciplinary Rules to registered practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered patent practitioners are subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A respondent's registration status subjects them to the Code of Professional Responsibility and related disciplinary regulations; the Final Order states that Respondent is a registered patent agent (with registration number) and thereby covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for discipline: conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: A violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) (engaging in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice) supports disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Respondent acknowledged the violation based on stipulated facts (in this case involvement in a patent-holding company’s litigation that resulted in malicious prosecution/abuse of process sanctions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction structure: suspension, stay, and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: The imposed sanction can be a suspension for a specified period (here, three months) that is immediately stayed, with the practitioner placed on a probationary period of equal length during which practice is permitted unless the stay is lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order may suspend the effective suspension by staying it and imposing probation; while the stay remains in effect the practitioner may continue to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure for alleged noncompliance during stay
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that the respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during the relevant period, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause why the stay should not be lifted and suspension imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order to Show Cause must be sent to the respondent at the last address of record furnished pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a), and the respondent is granted fifteen (15) days to respond to the Order to Show Cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to USPTO Director to lift stay and impose suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: After the 15-day response period, if the OED Director still believes noncompliance occurred, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director the Order to Show Cause, the respondent's response (if any), and evidence supporting the alleged noncompliance, and request that the Director lift the stay and suspend the respondent for up to the original suspension period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director’s submission to the USPTO Director triggers consideration of immediate lifting of the stay and imposition of suspension for the violation set forth in the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of lift and limitation on review: suspension takes immediate effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director lifts the stay and suspends the respondent and the respondent seeks review of that Director's decision, such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the immediate suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A review of the Director’s decision to lift a stay does not stay the suspension; the suspension remains effective pending any review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and public notice obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and give notice of the discipline and reasons to the public pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order must be posted electronically in the OED Reading Room URL and public notice requirements of § 11.59 must be followed to disseminate discipline information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice content requirements (Notice of Stayed Suspension example)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Stayed Suspension in the Official Gazette must identify the practitioner (name and registration number), state the sanction (suspension stayed and probation), cite the violated regulation (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5)), summarize the misconduct (e.g., sanctions for malicious prosecution/abuse of process), note any pertinent representations (e.g., indemnification), and identify statutory/regulatory bases and where disciplinary decisions are posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order includes an explicit example Notice of Stayed Suspension showing the level of detail expected in Official Gazette notices and the items to be disclosed publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to notify affected third parties and file proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a)(4), the respondent must provide, within thirty (30) days of the Final Order date, a copy of the Final Order to specified affected parties (here, Hypercom Corporation) and file, within forty-five (45) days of the Final Order date, an affidavit and corroborating documents (e.g., copies of the letters) with the OED Director stating compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order sets strict deadlines for notification to affected parties and requires corroborating proof filed with OED to demonstrate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational consequences of suspension for USPTO systems and credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: If the stay is lifted and the respondent is suspended, the USPTO shall promptly dissociate the respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates; the respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate or obtain any new until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension triggers technical and access actions by the USPTO to prevent practice before the Office (removal from customer numbers/PKI and prohibition on using/obtaining them until reinstatement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional application of certain regulatory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60 do not apply with respect to the suspension unless the stay of the suspension is lifted and the respondent is suspended pursuant to the stay-lift provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain regulatory procedures (the cited sections) apply only if the stay is lifted and the respondent is actually suspended; while the stay is in effect those provisions are inapplicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may seek additional discipline for the misconduct causing stay-lift
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the settlement/final order prevents the Office from seeking discipline against the respondent in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57 for the misconduct that caused the stay to be lifted and the respondent to be suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order preserves the Office’s right to pursue separate disciplinary action (under the listed regulatory provisions) for the underlying misconduct that leads to lifting the stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the disciplinary record in future matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, shall be considered (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor in determining discipline and/or to rebut any statement or representation by or on the respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly states that the record may be used both to aggravate future discipline and to rebut respondent assertions in later proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and the respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the settlement agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement/final order contains an express provision that each side bears its own costs (no fee shifting in this settlement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement as full resolution of disciplinary claims (with stipulated facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Proposed Settlement Agreement that resolves all disciplinary action arising from stipulated facts can be approved and the Final Order will set forth the stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions to resolve the disciplinary complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order reflects that the parties submitted stipulated facts and agreed sanctions; approval by the Director converts the settlement into an enforceable Final Order.
